name: The memorable line
what_it_does: Every section earns one line a reader could repeat: a sound bite, a reversal (not X but Y), a short line with rhythm or rhyme. It can be new; it does not have to remake David's line, but it must say what the section says.

name: Open inviting, not arguing
what_it_does: Openings are heartfelt and human before they are rigorous: a person, a moment, a wound, a question the reader already carries. The proof waits underneath. The reader should lean in, not brace.

name: Two things that should never be in the same room
what_it_does: An analogy between two things from unrelated worlds that explain each other. Always state the mapping (this part = that part) and where it stops holding, so it stays an honest analogy and never pretends to be a proof.

name: Situate it
what_it_does: Give the abstract idea somewhere to stand: a place, a moment, an object in the reader's world (a hospital hallway, a kitchen table, a courtroom, a field at dusk). Ground before you climb.

name: Never claim more than the section does
what_it_does: A gate, not a technique. No option and no memorable line may claim more than the original section claims. A beautiful line that overstates is a liability.
